Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Tower Bridge: Its steel frame is clad in stone to blend in with the nearby Tower of London, and its upper walkways were later closed, then reopened as a museum.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Brooklyn Bridge: Its stone towers rise above the East River. Chief engineer Washington Roebling was left bedridden by decompression sickness during construction.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Forth Bridge: This cantilever railway bridge in Scotland opened in 1890, and 'painting the Forth Bridge' became an expression for a never-ending job.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Erasmus Bridge, Rotterdam: This cable-stayed bridge's asymmetrical pylon earned it the nickname 'The Swan' among the people of Rotterdam.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Humber Bridge: For 16 years after opening in 1981, this was the longest single-span suspension bridge in the world.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Øresund Bridge: The bridge links Denmark and Sweden and starred in the Scandinavian crime drama 'The Bridge', which opens with a body found at its midpoint.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Golden Gate Bridge: Its color, International Orange, was chosen so the bridge shows up in San Francisco's frequent fog and also looks good against the hills.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Great Belt East Bridge: Denmark's Great Belt link has a main span of about 1,600 meters, among the longest in the world, and carries road traffic over the strait.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Akashi Kaikyō Bridge: This Japanese bridge has the world's longest suspension span, nearly 2 km. In 1995 the Kobe earthquake stretched it by about a meter during construction.
Heights of bridge towers and pylons.Millau Viaduct: The world's tallest bridge, its masts reach higher than the Eiffel Tower, and it floats over a valley in southern France.

Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.Martius: The year began in March, named for the god Mars, which is why September, October, November and December still carry numbers.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.Aprilis: The name may come from the Latin aperire, 'to open', as buds do in spring, though ancient writers disagreed on its origin.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.Maius: Probably named for Maia, a goddess of growth, though some Roman writers linked the name to maiores, meaning elders.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.Iunius: Named for Juno, goddess of marriage, which is why Romans, like many people since, considered it a lucky month for weddings.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.Quintilis: It means 'fifth' in Latin. Renamed July after Julius Caesar, who was born in it, it was moved to be the seventh month.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.Sextilis: The 'sixth' month was renamed August in 8 BC in honor of the emperor Augustus.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.September: Its name means 'seventh', though it is now the ninth month, a leftover from the ten-month Roman year.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.October: Octo means 'eight' in Latin, and the month kept its name even after it became the tenth month of the year.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.November: Its name comes from the Latin for 'nine', and it stuck even after January and February joined the year.
Months of Rome's original ten-month cale.December: The Roman winter festival Saturnalia took place in December, with feasts and gift-giving that shaped later holiday traditions.

Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.A partridge in a pear tree: The song's only line without a count. Its earliest known printing is from the 1780 English children's book Mirth without Mischief.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Turtle doves: European turtle doves have declined sharply and are now listed as vulnerable. Their soft purring song is a classic sound of summer.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.French hens: Probably plump hens from France, such as the Houdan or Faverolles, which are old French breeds known for table quality.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Calling birds: Originally 'colly birds', an old word for blackbirds, since 'colly' means coal-black. The line was changed to 'calling' over time.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Gold rings: Often thought to mean ring-necked pheasants rather than jewelry, which would make them the only gold in the song a bird, though it's debated.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Geese a-laying: Geese usually lay in late winter and spring, so six laying in midwinter would be a surprise on any farm.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Swans a-swimming: Swans were once royal property in England, and the Crown still claims unmarked mute swans on open water.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Maids a-milking: Add up every gift in every verse of the song and you get 364, one for each day of the year apart from one.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Lords a-leaping: The modern tune most people sing was arranged by Frederic Austin in 1909, and his version added the drawn-out 'five gold rings'.
Gifts in \"The Twelve Days of Christmas\.Drummers drumming: The twelve days run from Christmas Day to 5 January, called Twelfth Night, traditionally the end of the Christmas season.

Legendary motor races, by first running.Targa Florio: This Sicilian road race ran through mountain villages, and the Targa Florio was one of the oldest in sports-car racing, lasting until 1977.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Isle of Man TT: Riders still race on closed public roads around the island's 60 km Mountain Course, one of the most dangerous circuits in the world.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Pikes Peak hill climb: Cars race about 12 miles and some 156 turns up a Colorado mountain, finishing at around 14,000 feet.
Legendary motor races, by first running.24 Hours of Le Mans: In 1966, Ford finally beat Ferrari here, a story told in the film Ford v Ferrari.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Mille Miglia: The name means thousand miles, and the road race through Italian towns ended in 1957 after a crash killed spectators.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Monaco Grand Prix: Winning here is part of motor racing's Triple Crown, along with the Indy 500 and Le Mans, and it is famously hard to overtake on the narrow streets.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Macau Grand Prix: This street race on a hillside circuit hosts Formula 3 and motorcycle events, and is known for its tight corners.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Daytona 500: NASCAR's biggest race, nicknamed the Great American Race, runs 500 miles on a 2.5-mile tri-oval in Florida.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Bahrain Grand Prix: It was the first Formula One race held in the Middle East.
Legendary motor races, by first running.Singapore Grand Prix: F1's first night race, held under floodlights, runs on a twisty street circuit in a tropical city-state.

Holidays through the calendar year.New Year's Day: Rome moved its new year to 1 January in 153 BC, when its consuls began taking office that day, and Julius Caesar's calendar later locked it in.
Holidays through the calendar year.Valentine's Day: It honours one or more early Christian martyrs named Valentine; the romantic link is often credited to Chaucer's poetry in the 1300s.
Holidays through the calendar year.St. Patrick's Day: Patrick was kidnapped from Roman Britain to Ireland as a teenager, and Chicago has dyed its river green for the holiday since 1962.
Holidays through the calendar year.Earth Day: The first Earth Day in 1970 drew about 20 million Americans into the streets and helped lead to the founding of the US EPA that year.
Holidays through the calendar year.US Independence Day: Congress voted for independence on 2 July 1776, and John Adams expected that date to be the one celebrated; the Declaration was adopted two days later.
Holidays through the calendar year.Bastille Day: It marks the 1789 storming of a Paris fortress-prison that held only seven prisoners but had become a hated symbol of royal power.
Holidays through the calendar year.Halloween: It grew from the Celtic festival Samhain and the eve of All Saints' Day; the first jack-o'-lanterns in Ireland were carved from turnips, not pumpkins.
Holidays through the calendar year.Guy Fawkes Night: Guy Fawkes was caught guarding barrels of gunpowder under Parliament in 1605, and Britons have burned bonfires and effigies every November since.
Holidays through the calendar year.Armistice Day: Fighting in World War I stopped at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month in 1918; the US later renamed the day Veterans Day.
Holidays through the calendar year.Christmas Day: The Gospels never give a date for the birth of Jesus; 25 December was settled on by the fourth century, and Puritan England once banned Christmas outright.

Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Lewis Wilson: He played Batman in a 1943 serial that introduced the Batcave, and the hero was shown fighting Japanese agents in wartime.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Robert Lowery: He took the cowl in the 1949 serial Batman and Robin, and he stayed the character's film face until the 1960s.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Adam West: His 1966 TV series spawned the on-screen Pow! and Bam! and a campy tone that Batman fans debated for decades.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Michael Keaton: When Tim Burton cast the comic actor in 1989, fans petitioned against it, but the film's success proved them wrong.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Kevin Conroy (voice): He voiced Batman in Batman: The Animated Series, long considered the definitive voice, and played the role for decades until he died in 2022.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Val Kilmer: He wore the suit in Batman Forever, directed by Joel Schumacher, which leaned toward bright neon styling.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.George Clooney: Batman and Robin was widely panned for its camp and its famous bat-nipple costumes, and Clooney himself later joked about it.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Christian Bale: Christopher Nolan's Batman Begins relaunched the character in 2005 with a grounded, darker tone.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Ben Affleck: He debuted in Batman v Superman as an older, battle-worn Batman, and later returned in the Justice League film.
Actors' first time as Batman on screen.Robert Pattinson: The 2022 film The Batman gives us a younger detective, in a noir story set in a rain-soaked Gotham.

Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Johann Sebastian Bach: Bach wrote over a thousand works, but it took Mendelssohn's 1829 revival of the St Matthew Passion to restore him to wide fame.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart: A child prodigy who composed at five, Mozart wrote over 600 works before dying at just 35.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Ludwig van Beethoven: He kept composing masterpieces, including the Ninth Symphony, after going almost completely deaf.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Frédéric Chopin: Born in Poland, he spent his career in Paris writing almost entirely for piano, and his heart was returned to Warsaw.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Pyotr Tchaikovsky: His ballets Swan Lake, The Nutcracker and Sleeping Beauty are staples, and his 1812 Overture famously calls for cannons.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.George Gershwin: He bridged jazz and classical in Rhapsody in Blue and wrote the opera Porgy and Bess before dying at 38.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Leonard Bernstein: He composed West Side Story and was the first American-born conductor to lead the New York Philharmonic.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.John Williams: With over 50 Oscar nominations, second only to Walt Disney, he scored Star Wars, Jaws and Harry Potter.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Andrew Lloyd Webber: Cats ran for 21 years in London, and he also composed The Phantom of the Opera and Evita.
Composers from Bach to blockbusters, by.Hans Zimmer: Largely self-taught on keyboards, he scored The Lion King, Inception and Dune, winning Oscars for the first and last.

Magnetic field strengths.Human brain activity: Neurons' electrical currents create tiny magnetic fields that MEG scanners detect with superconducting sensors.
Magnetic field strengths.Earth's magnetic field: The field comes from churning liquid iron in the outer core, and it shields us from the solar wind.
Magnetic field strengths.Fridge magnet: Most are flexible rubber with magnetic powder in plastic, weak enough that a few sheets of paper can overcome them.
Magnetic field strengths.Sunspot: Sunspots look dark because intense fields block heat flow from below, making them cooler than the surrounding surface.
Magnetic field strengths.Neodymium magnet: The strongest common permanent magnets, they can pinch intestines if swallowed in pairs, a real hazard.
Magnetic field strengths.Hospital MRI scanner: This is tens of thousands of times Earth's field, which is why loose metal objects can become projectiles.
Magnetic field strengths.Magnet that levitated a frog: Physicist Andre Geim levitated a live frog in 1997, work that earned him a joke Ig Nobel and later a real Nobel for graphene.
Magnetic field strengths.Strongest steady lab magnet: The 45 T hybrid magnet in Florida long held the record for strongest continuous field.
Magnetic field strengths.Neutron star: A neutron star squeezes more than a sun's mass into a city-sized ball, and the collapse amplifies its magnetism enormously.
Magnetic field strengths.Magnetar: These neutron stars have the strongest fields known, and a 2004 flare disturbed Earth's upper atmosphere from thousands of light-years away.

Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Vulcanized rubber: Goodyear reportedly dropped rubber mixed with sulphur onto a hot stove and found it had become tough and elastic.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Mauve dye: William Perkin, aged 18, was trying to make quinine when he got a purple dye, launching the synthetic dye industry.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.X-rays: Rontgen noticed a screen glowing across his lab while testing a cathode-ray tube and named the rays X for unknown.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Radioactivity: Henri Becquerel found uranium salts fogged photographic plates even in the dark, revealing invisible radiation.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Penicillin: Alexander Fleming came back from holiday to find mould had killed the bacteria in a dish he had left out.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Teflon: Roy Plunkett found a gas cylinder had turned its contents into a slippery white solid, PTFE.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Super Glue: Harry Coover found cyanoacrylate too sticky for gun sights, then spotted its power as an adhesive.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Microwave cooking: Percy Spencer noticed a candy bar had melted in his pocket near a radar tube and then tried popcorn.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Cosmic microwave background: Penzias and Wilson tried to remove a persistent hiss from their antenna, even cleaning away pigeon droppings; it was the Big Bang's afterglow.
Happy accidents: when these were stumble.Pulsars: Jocelyn Bell Burnell spotted a regular pulse of radio waves, jokingly labelled LGM-1 for little green men, before pulsars were understood.

Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Windscreen wiper: Mary Anderson patented the first windshield wiper in 1903 after watching a streetcar driver struggle in a snowstorm in New York.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Ford Model T: By 1925 Ford's moving assembly line turned out a Model T about every 10 seconds, and the price fell from 850 dollars to under 300.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Electric starter: Charles Kettering's invention replaced the dangerous hand crank, and it debuted on the 1912 Cadillac.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Electric traffic light: The first electric one was installed in Cleveland in 1914, with red and green lights and a buzzer, and cars before had a human officer.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Car radio: Motorola's name, a blend of 'motor' and 'Victrola', came from the company's first big product, a radio built for cars in 1930.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Parking meter: The first one in the world was installed in Oklahoma City in 1935, and it helped solve downtown parking congestion.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Breathalyzer: Indiana police captain Robert Borkenstein's device measured alcohol in a driver's breath by a chemical color change, and it replaced slow blood tests.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Three-point seatbelt: Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin created this safer belt, and Volvo then gave the patent away freely, which probably saved a million lives.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Catalytic converter: Made mandatory on US cars from 1975 to cut smog, it coats a ceramic honeycomb with precious metals such as platinum and rhodium.
Car inventions, by when they hit the roa.Toyota Prius: Toyota's gasoline-electric hybrid went on sale in Japan in 1997, and it later became a bestseller worldwide.

Older than you'd think: first invented.Vending machine: Hero of Alexandria described a coin-operated machine that dispensed holy water in the first century AD.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Flush toilet: Sir John Harington built one for Queen Elizabeth I, who was his godmother.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Submarine: Cornelius Drebbel demonstrated one on the Thames, rowed by oarsmen, in 1620.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Chainsaw (for surgery): Scottish doctors designed it to cut through bone in childbirth, long before it was used on trees.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Selfie: Robert Cornelius took the first photographic self-portrait in 1839, in his family's shop in Philadelphia.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Fax machine: Alexander Bain patented it in 1843, decades before the telephone existed.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Contact lens: Adolf Fick made the first glass ones in 1888, testing them on rabbits and human volunteers.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Bubble wrap: Created in 1957 as textured wallpaper, it was only later turned into packing material.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Video game: William Higinbotham made Tennis for Two at Brookhaven National Laboratory in 1958, on an oscilloscope.
Older than you'd think: first invented.Mobile phone call: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the call from a New York street, phoning a rival at Bell Labs.

World capitals from north to south.Reykjavík: Iceland's capital is the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state, and nearly all its homes are heated by geothermal energy.
World capitals from north to south.Oslo: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in this city, unlike the other Nobel prizes, which are presented in Stockholm.
World capitals from north to south.Moscow: Its metro stations are lavish, with chandeliers and marble, built in the Stalin era as palaces for the people.
World capitals from north to south.London: The Greenwich Meridian, zero degrees longitude, passes just through the city, which is why time zones are measured from here.
World capitals from north to south.Paris: Paris sits farther north than Montreal, which surprises many people given how mild winters are in comparison.
World capitals from north to south.Rome: The world's smallest country, Vatican City, sits entirely inside it, with its own postal service and its own railway station.
World capitals from north to south.Cairo: The largest city in the Arab world, with the Giza pyramids rising at its edge, the oldest of the ancient wonders still standing.
World capitals from north to south.Nairobi: Though almost on the equator, it sits about 1,800 m up, so it stays cool, and a national park with lions borders the city.
World capitals from north to south.Canberra: It was a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne, designed by the American architect Walter Burley Griffin, who won a contest.
World capitals from north to south.Wellington: It is the world's southernmost national capital, and it is famous for its wind, which makes the city feel colder than it is.

Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Honolulu: Hawaii is the one US state that doesn't change its clocks, so it's UTC-10 all year.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Anchorage: Most of Alaska uses this zone, though the western Aleutian Islands follow Hawaii time instead.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Vancouver: It shares a zone with Los Angeles and Seattle, and the clocks change on the same days.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Phoenix: Arizona skips daylight saving time, except in the Navajo Nation, which observes it.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Mexico City: Mexico abolished daylight saving time in 2022, so the capital stays at UTC-6 year-round.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Lima: Peru uses UTC-5 all year, as do Colombia and Ecuador, and none of them change their clocks.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Caracas: Venezuela shifted by half an hour in 2007 and went back in 2016, so it now sits on UTC-4.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.St. John's, Newfoundland: Newfoundland's half-hour offset is unusual; its clocks run 30 minutes ahead of the rest of Atlantic Canada.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Buenos Aires: Argentina sits at UTC-3 year-round, with the sun rising early in the east of the country.
Time zones of the Americas (standard tim.Azores (Ponta Delgada): These Portuguese islands run one hour behind the mainland, and at UTC-1 they sit closest to UTC here.

Programming languages by first release.Fortran: John Backus's team at IBM created it. The name means Formula Translation, and it still runs weather and physics simulations.
Programming languages by first release.BASIC: Dartmouth's Kemeny and Kurtz made it for beginners, and Microsoft's first product was a BASIC for the Altair.
Programming languages by first release.C: Dennis Ritchie created it at Bell Labs to rewrite the Unix operating system.
Programming languages by first release.C++: Bjarne Stroustrup began it as C with Classes. The name is a joke on the ++ increment operator.
Programming languages by first release.Perl: Larry Wall's language earned the nickname the duct tape of the internet for gluing systems together.
Programming languages by first release.Python: Guido van Rossum named it after Monty Python, not the snake.
Programming languages by first release.Java: Originally called Oak, it promised write once, run anywhere. The final name was inspired by coffee.
Programming languages by first release.C#: Microsoft's language was led by Anders Hejlsberg, who also created Turbo Pascal.
Programming languages by first release.Go: Designed at Google by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike and Ken Thompson, co-creator of Unix.
Programming languages by first release.Swift: Apple's language replaced Objective-C as the main way to build iPhone apps; Chris Lattner started it in secret.

Wes Anderson films by release.Bottle Rocket: Expanded from a short film, it launched Owen and Luke Wilson's careers alongside Anderson's.
Wes Anderson films by release.Rushmore: Jason Schwartzman plays Max Fischer, a teenage overachiever, in the film that helped revive Bill Murray's career.
Wes Anderson films by release.The Royal Tenenbaums: This family tragicomedy earned Anderson his first Oscar nomination, for original screenplay.
Wes Anderson films by release.The Life Aquatic: Bill Murray plays a Cousteau-like oceanographer, while musician Seu Jorge sings David Bowie songs in Portuguese.
Wes Anderson films by release.Fantastic Mr. Fox: Anderson's first stop-motion film, adapted from Roald Dahl's children's novel.
Wes Anderson films by release.Moonrise Kingdom: Set on a fictional New England island in 1965, it opened the Cannes Film Festival.
Wes Anderson films by release.The Grand Budapest Hotel: It won four Oscars, was nominated for Best Picture, and drew inspiration from the writings of Stefan Zweig.
Wes Anderson films by release.Isle of Dogs: This second stop-motion film, set in a future Japan, won Anderson the Silver Bear for Best Director in Berlin.
Wes Anderson films by release.The French Dispatch: An anthology tribute to a fictional magazine, loosely modeled on The New Yorker.
Wes Anderson films by release.Asteroid City: A 1950s desert story with a play inside it, filmed in Spain rather than in an actual American desert.

Language academies, by founding year.Accademia della Crusca: Named for 'bran', it aimed to sift pure language from chaff, and its 1612 dictionary became a landmark for Italian.
Language academies, by founding year.Académie française: Created under Cardinal Richelieu, it has 40 members, called the immortals, and guards French through its dictionary.
Language academies, by founding year.Real Academia Española: Its motto is 'limpia, fija y da esplendor', cleans, sets and gives splendor, and it works with sister academies across the Spanish-speaking world.
Language academies, by founding year.Swedish Academy: Founded by King Gustav III with 18 chairs, it also chooses the winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Language academies, by founding year.Hungarian Academy: It was launched after nobleman István Széchenyi pledged a year's income to it, and promotes Hungarian language and learning.
Language academies, by founding year.Brazilian Academy of Letters: Modeled on the French academy, it has 40 members, and the novelist Machado de Assis was its first president.
Language academies, by founding year.Royal Galician Academy: It regulates Galician, a Romance language of northwest Spain that is closely related to Portuguese.
Language academies, by founding year.Basque Language Academy: Basque is a language isolate unrelated to any other living language, and this body, Euskaltzaindia, sets its standard forms.
Language academies, by founding year.Academy of the Hebrew Language: It succeeded the Hebrew Language Committee begun by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda in 1890, and coins modern words for the revived language.
Language academies, by founding year.National Institute of Korean: It publishes Korea's standard dictionary and rules for romanization, and the alphabet Hangul has its own annual holiday.

Number trivia: which value is biggest?.5th triangular number: Fifteen is a triangular number: 1+2+3+4+5. Ten bowling pins are the fourth triangular number, with 15 balls in a pool rack.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.8th prime: Nineteen is the eighth prime, and it is also the number of years in the Metonic cycle, after which moon phases fall on the same dates.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.Primes below 100 (count): There are exactly 25 primes below 100, which means one in every four numbers up to 100 is prime.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.2nd perfect number: 28 is the second perfect number: its divisors 1, 2, 4, 7 and 14 add up to itself, and it is close to a lunar month.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.10th prime: Twenty-nine is the tenth prime, and it is also the number of days in a leap-year February.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.6th square number: Thirty-six is both a perfect square and a triangular number, and there are 36 combinations of two dice.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.4th cube number: Sixty-four is both a square and a cube, and it is the number of squares on a chessboard.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.4th Mersenne prime: 127 is the fourth Mersenne prime, 2 to the power 7 minus 1, and its 128-value neighbor is the number of ASCII characters.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.12th Fibonacci number: 144 is the largest Fibonacci number that's also a perfect square besides 1, and it's 12 squared.
Number trivia: which value is biggest?.3rd perfect number: 496 is the third perfect number, and it's the sum of its proper divisors, found from Euclid's formula.

Beauty brands, by founding year.Avon: It began as the California Perfume Company, and sold door to door through 'Avon ladies'. The name came from Shakespeare's Avon.
Beauty brands, by founding year.L'Oréal: Chemist Eugène Schueller started it by selling a safe synthetic hair dye to Paris hairdressers.
Beauty brands, by founding year.Nivea: Its name comes from the Latin for snow. The round blue tin of cream debuted in 1911 and has barely changed since.
Beauty brands, by founding year.Maybelline: Founder T. L. Williams reportedly made a mascara for his sister Mabel from coal dust and petroleum jelly, which gave the brand its name.
Beauty brands, by founding year.Revlon: Charles Revson started with opaque nail enamel, and the name merges his surname with the L of partner Charles Lachman.
Beauty brands, by founding year.Estée Lauder: She started by selling skin creams made by her chemist uncle, and built a global empire on a gift-with-purchase promotion.
Beauty brands, by founding year.Clinique: It was marketed as the first dermatologist-guided, allergy-tested, fragrance-free line, after a magazine feature about skin care.
Beauty brands, by founding year.The Body Shop: Anita Roddick opened a first shop in Brighton, England, and encouraged customers to refill bottles and avoid animal testing.
Beauty brands, by founding year.MAC Cosmetics: Two Toronto makeup artists founded it for professionals, and the name stands for Make-up Art Cosmetics.
Beauty brands, by founding year.Fenty Beauty: Rihanna launched with 40 foundation shades, so many that rivals expanded their ranges, a shift people call the 'Fenty effect'.

Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Games to win a tennis set: In 2010 at Wimbledon, John Isner and Nicolas Mahut played a match lasting over 11 hours, since the final set had no tiebreak.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Hurdles in a sprint hurdles: Modern hurdles tip over when hit, a 1930s design that replaced older fixed barriers.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Points to win a ping-pong game: Games were played to 21 until 2001, when the shorter 11-point format arrived to make matches faster and more TV-friendly.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Players on a Ryder Cup team: The golf contest is named after Samuel Ryder, an English seed merchant who donated the trophy.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Max clubs in a golf bag: The limit arrived in 1938, since some players had been carrying over 20 clubs.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Reds on a snooker table: Potting a red then a black fifteen times and then clearing the colours gives the maximum break of 147.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Holes in a round of golf: St Andrews once had 22 holes, but in 1764 it merged some, and the 18-hole round became the standard.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Points to win a badminton game: Games were to 15 until the rally-scoring switch in 2006. The sport's name comes from Badminton House in England.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Points to win a volleyball set: William Morgan invented it in 1895 as 'Mintonette', a gentler game for older businessmen than basketball.
Magic numbers from the rulebooks.Minutes in an NFL game: Though the clock runs 60 minutes, studies of broadcasts found the ball is in actual play for only around 11 minutes.

When these famous documents were written.Luther's 95 Theses: Martin Luther's challenge to the sale of indulgences spread across Germany in weeks thanks to the printing press, though the door-nailing story is debated.
When these famous documents were written.King James Bible: About 47 scholars produced it for King James I, and it gave English phrases like the skin of my teeth.
When these famous documents were written.Mayflower Compact: Signed aboard ship by 41 men before landing at Cape Cod, it was an early agreement to govern themselves by majority rule.
When these famous documents were written.English Bill of Rights: It limited the monarch's power and banned cruel and unusual punishments, a phrase that returned in the US Constitution.
When these famous documents were written.Declaration of Independence: It was adopted on 4 July, but most delegates signed on 2 August, and Thomas Jefferson was its main author.
When these famous documents were written.Rights of Man (France): Formally the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, it was drafted in the Revolution's first months and still anchors French law.
When these famous documents were written.Communist Manifesto: Marx and Engels published it in London as a slim pamphlet, and its opening line about a spectre haunting Europe is world famous.
When these famous documents were written.Emancipation Proclamation: It freed enslaved people only in Confederate-held areas; the 13th Amendment ended slavery nationwide in 1865.
When these famous documents were written.UN Human Rights Declaration: Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the drafting committee, and the text is now one of the most translated documents, in over 500 languages.
When these famous documents were written.Kyoto Protocol: Adopted in Kyoto, it set binding emission cuts for developed countries, though the United States never ratified it.

Plants from tiny to towering.Wolffia (watermeal): This is the smallest flowering plant, rootless and food-like; in parts of Southeast Asia it is eaten as a high-protein green.
Plants from tiny to towering.Duckweed: Floating mats of it can double their mass in a couple of days, so ponds can turn green almost overnight.
Plants from tiny to towering.Moss: It has no true roots or vascular system, and peat bogs built from sphagnum moss lock away a vast share of soil carbon.
Plants from tiny to towering.Clover: Clover works with bacteria in its roots to fix nitrogen, so farmers plant it to fertilise soil for free.
Plants from tiny to towering.Tulip: Tulips came from Central Asia and Turkey, and in the 1630s a single bulb in the Netherlands could cost more than a house.
Plants from tiny to towering.Sunflower: Young sunflowers follow the sun across the sky, and mature ones settle facing east to warm up for bees.
Plants from tiny to towering.Banana plant: It is not a tree but a giant herb whose false trunk is made of tightly wrapped leaf bases.
Plants from tiny to towering.Saguaro cactus: A saguaro may not grow its first arm until it is 50 to 75 years old, and can store tonnes of water.
Plants from tiny to towering.Coconut palm: Coconuts float and can drift across oceans, which helped palms colonise tropical islands, and palms have no bark or growth rings.
Plants from tiny to towering.Coast redwood: The tallest known tree, named Hyperion, is a coast redwood of about 116 metres, standing in a secret location in California.

Turning points in Russian history.Romanov dynasty begins: Michael Romanov was chosen tsar after the chaotic Time of Troubles, and his family ruled Russia for 304 years.
Turning points in Russian history.St. Petersburg founded: Peter the Great built his 'window to Europe' on marshland at huge human cost, and it was the capital for two centuries.
Turning points in Russian history.Pugachev's Rebellion: A Cossack claiming to be the murdered Tsar Peter III led a vast peasant uprising that Catherine the Great crushed.
Turning points in Russian history.Napoleon enters Moscow: He found the city largely abandoned and soon in flames, and the lack of surrender plus a brutal winter retreat wrecked his army.
Turning points in Russian history.Decembrist revolt: Liberal army officers rebelled after Alexander I's death, demanding reform; Nicholas I crushed them and hanged five leaders.
Turning points in Russian history.Serfs emancipated: Alexander II's edict freed millions of peasants, but they owed redemption payments for decades, so unrest continued.
Turning points in Russian history.Bloody Sunday: Troops fired on peaceful workers petitioning the tsar in St Petersburg, shattering trust in Nicholas II and igniting the 1905 revolution.
Turning points in Russian history.Romanov family executed: Nicholas II, his wife and their five children were shot by Bolsheviks in Yekaterinburg; their remains were found decades later.
Turning points in Russian history.Stalin dies: His death ended about a quarter-century of terror and opened the way for Khrushchev's partial 'thaw'.
Turning points in Russian history.Moscow hosts the Olympics: The US and many allies boycotted over the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan; Misha the bear mascot famously appeared to cry at the closing.

Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Stapes, the smallest bone: The stirrup-shaped stapes in the ear is the body's smallest bone, passing sound vibrations to the inner ear.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Eyelash: Eyelashes live for a few months before falling out and regrowing, and touching one triggers a blink.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Ear canal: The canal shapes and amplifies certain sounds, boosting the frequencies important for speech.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Fallopian tube: Eggs travel along these tubes, where fertilization usually happens, swept along by hair-like cilia.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Esophagus: Muscles squeeze food down, so you can swallow even while upside down.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Spinal cord: It ends well short of the spine's base, around the lower back, where a bundle of nerves continues downward.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Large intestine: Wider than the small intestine, it houses trillions of bacteria that help ferment fiber.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Uncoiled DNA of one cell: Stretched out, the DNA from all your cells would reach to the Sun and back many times.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Tallest man ever (Wadlow): Robert Wadlow of Illinois stood 8 ft 11 in and kept growing until his death at 22.
Long and short: lengths in and of the bo.Small intestine: Despite its name for being narrow, it's the longest part of the gut, folded to absorb nutrients.

Polygons by number of sides.Triangle: The triangle is the only rigid polygon: a frame made from three bars can't be squashed without breaking, which is why bridges and roofs use them.
Polygons by number of sides.Square: A square is a rectangle and a rhombus at once, and a diamond on a playing card or baseball field is just a square turned on a corner.
Polygons by number of sides.Pentagon: Home to the US Department of Defense, the Pentagon building in Virginia is shaped like this, and it's among the world's largest office buildings.
Polygons by number of sides.Hexagon: Honeybees build their combs from it because this shape tiles with no gaps, using the least wax for the most storage.
Polygons by number of sides.Heptagon: A regular one can't be drawn exactly with just compass and straightedge, and the British 50p coin is a seven-sided shape.
Polygons by number of sides.Octagon: Stop signs use this shape in much of the world, and a regular one has interior angles of 135 degrees.
Polygons by number of sides.Nonagon: Its name mixes Latin and Greek, which purists dislike, so mathematicians often call it an enneagon instead.
Polygons by number of sides.Decagon: Its interior angles add to 1,440 degrees, and its name uses the Greek word for ten.
Polygons by number of sides.Dodecagon: Britain's old brass threepence coin had twelve sides, a shape picked to stop it being confused with the sixpence.
Polygons by number of sides.Icosagon: The twenty-sided figure shares its Greek root with the icosahedron, the 20-sided dice known as the d20 of role-playing games.

Science moments of the 1900s.Wright brothers fly: The first flight at Kitty Hawk lasted only 12 seconds and covered about 36 m, shorter than a modern jumbo jet's wingspan.
Science moments of the 1900s.Special relativity: Einstein published four groundbreaking papers that year while working as a patent clerk in Bern.
Science moments of the 1900s.Penicillin discovered: Alexander Fleming noticed that mold had killed bacteria in a dish he left out during a holiday.
Science moments of the 1900s.Nuclear fission: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann split uranium, and Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch explained it; she never won the Nobel.
Science moments of the 1900s.DNA double helix: Watson and Crick built their model using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image, Photo 51, which they saw without her knowledge.
Science moments of the 1900s.Sputnik launched: The 83 kg metal ball beeped for about three weeks and set off the space race.
Science moments of the 1900s.First laser: Theodore Maiman's ruby device at Hughes Laboratories was first called a solution looking for a problem.
Science moments of the 1900s.Moon landing: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon, with onboard computers far less powerful than a modern phone.
Science moments of the 1900s.Dolly the sheep: The cloned sheep, born in Scotland, was named after singer Dolly Parton, because the cells came from a mammary gland.
Science moments of the 1900s.Human genome completed: The Human Genome Project took 13 years to read about 3 billion DNA letters.

Countries by population density.Mongolia: The least densely populated sovereign country, where about half the people live in Ulaanbaatar and horses outnumber people.
Countries by population density.Canada: Most people live within about 160 km of the US border, so the real density is much higher in the south.
Countries by population density.Russia: It is the largest country on Earth, and most of Siberia is nearly empty.
Countries by population density.United States: Alaska has about one person per square kilometre, while New Jersey has roughly 470.
Countries by population density.China: About 94 percent of people live east of the Hu Line, a diagonal from Heihe to Tengchong.
Countries by population density.United Kingdom: England is among the most densely populated large countries in Europe, with more than 400 people per square kilometre.
Countries by population density.Netherlands: A big share of the land was reclaimed from the sea as polders, and about a quarter lies below sea level.
Countries by population density.Bangladesh: More than 170 million people live in a country about the size of Iowa, mostly on the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta.
Countries by population density.Singapore: This city-state has grown by land reclamation and builds up, since there is little room to spread out.
Countries by population density.Monaco: The tiny principality is the second-smallest country in the world, after the Vatican, at about two square kilometres.

Disaster movies by release.Airport: Arthur Hailey's novel became this hit, which earned Helen Hayes an Oscar and kicked off the disaster boom and its sequels.
Disaster movies by release.The Poseidon Adventure: Its upside-down luxury liner was a hit, and its song 'The Morning After' won an Oscar for Best Original Song.
Disaster movies by release.The Towering Inferno: Two rival studios, Fox and Warner Bros., teamed up to make it, which also meant Steve McQueen and Paul Newman could share the screen.
Disaster movies by release.Twister: Its 'Dorothy' device, which fires sensors into the storm, was inspired by a real research tool known as TOTO.
Disaster movies by release.Dante's Peak: The volcano story shared its year with a rival film, Volcano, and the two competed in cinemas.
Disaster movies by release.Armageddon: Aerosmith's 'I Don't Want to Miss a Thing' came from this film; its star Liv Tyler is the daughter of the band's Steven Tyler.
Disaster movies by release.The Day After Tomorrow: Scientists doubted its sudden freeze, as the planet could never turn cold in days, but it was a big hit worldwide.
Disaster movies by release.San Andreas: The San Andreas Fault is roughly 1,200 km long and runs through California, and geologists do expect a major quake there.
Disaster movies by release.Geostorm: It became a notorious flop after expensive reshoots, and Gerard Butler headed the cast.
Disaster movies by release.Don't Look Up: Adam McKay's satire of ignored warnings about a comet became one of Netflix's most-watched films soon after release.

Notorious tornadoes, in order.Great Natchez Tornado: It hit Natchez, Mississippi, killing more than 300 people, many on boats on the river, making it among the deadliest ever in the US.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.Tri-State Tornado: The deadliest in US history killed 695 people and travelled about 350 km across Missouri, Illinois and Indiana in a few hours.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.Woodward, Oklahoma: It was part of a deadly April outbreak across the Plains, and killed well over a hundred people as it struck.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.The Super Outbreak: Over 148 tornadoes hit 13 US states in about 18 hours, among the largest outbreaks ever recorded.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.Daulatpur–Saturia: It killed about 1,300 people in Bangladesh, which is thought to be the deadliest tornado in history.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.Bridge Creek–Moore: A mobile radar clocked winds of about 300 mph in this storm, the highest wind speed ever measured on Earth.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.Joplin, Missouri: An EF5 that killed about 160 people, it was the deadliest US tornado since modern record keeping began in 1950.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.El Reno, Oklahoma: At roughly 4 km wide, it was the widest tornado ever recorded, and it killed several storm chasers, including Tim Samaras.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.Mayfield, Kentucky: A December tornado outbreak is unusual, and this long-track one devastated the Kentucky town, including a candle factory.
Notorious tornadoes, in order.Rolling Fork, Mississippi: This EF4 struck the small Mississippi Delta town in March 2023, one of the strongest tornadoes of that year.

Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Electron: J.J. Thomson found it in 1897 through cathode rays, the first subatomic particle discovered.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Photon (light quantum): Einstein proposed that light comes in packets, which earned his Nobel; the word photon was coined in 1926.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Proton: Ernest Rutherford found it by knocking hydrogen nuclei from nitrogen, and later named it.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Neutron: James Chadwick found it, electrically neutral and so hard to detect, winning the 1935 Nobel.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Muon: Found in cosmic rays and about 207 times heavier than an electron, it made physicist Rabi ask, who ordered that?
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Neutrino (detected): Wolfgang Pauli predicted it in 1930, and Cowan and Reines detected it near a nuclear reactor.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Quarks (proposed): Murray Gell-Mann took the name from a line in Finnegans Wake: Three quarks for Muster Mark.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.W and Z bosons: Found at CERN, they confirmed the electroweak theory, and Rubbia and van der Meer won the Nobel in 1984.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Top quark: Found at Fermilab, it is the heaviest known elementary particle, about as heavy as a gold atom.
Subatomic particles, by when they were f.Higgs boson: CERN's Large Hadron Collider found it, and physicists dislike its nickname, the God particle.

How a fossil forms.Animal dies: Few animals ever become fossils; the odds are tiny. The best chances are in places where bodies are buried quickly, like seabeds, lakes and river floods.
How a fossil forms.Mud quickly covers it: Fast burial protects the body from scavengers and decay. Many of the best fossils come from sudden events, like mudslides.
How a fossil forms.Soft parts rot away: Skin, muscle and organs usually decay, so most fossils are of hard parts like bones, teeth and shells. Rare sites also preserve soft tissue.
How a fossil forms.More layers pile on top: Over thousands of years, sediment builds up, and its weight squeezes the layers underneath. Deeper layers are normally older.
How a fossil forms.Minerals seep into the bones: Groundwater carries minerals into the bone's pores, which gradually replace the original material. The result is a stone copy of the bone.
How a fossil forms.Layers harden into rock: Sediments are compressed and cemented together into sedimentary rock, such as sandstone, shale or limestone. Fossils are almost always found in such rocks.
How a fossil forms.Rock is pushed upward: Plate movements lift ancient seabeds into mountains, which is why marine fossils turn up at the tops of high peaks, even on Everest.
How a fossil forms.Wind and rain wear it down: Erosion slowly strips away the rock and exposes the fossil. Cliffs and badlands are good places to find them, as erosion keeps revealing new ones.
How a fossil forms.Fossil hunter spots it: Many famous finds were made by amateurs. Mary Anning, a young woman in Dorset, found some of the first ichthyosaur and plesiosaur skeletons in the early 1800s.
How a fossil forms.Goes on show in a museum: Specimens are carefully cleaned and studied by palaeontologists. Some dinosaur skeletons on display are mostly casts, while the originals stay in storage.
